text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday announced a Federal Government push for increases in minimum wages for low-paid workers of A$24 a week over the next three years. The across the board wage reforms have been opposed by employers, yet Howard believes the decision will prove wrong any Labor Party claims that the Coalition Government is indifferent to the interests of the low-paid. Page 1.

The Federal Government is actively looking to negotiate a deal with the United States in an attempt to protect two of the country's largest manufacturing industries, cars and textiles. Unless agreement can be reached this week, a U.S. complaint will automatically trigger a formal disputes procedure in the World Trade Organisation, the result of which may be savage trade sanctions. Page 1.

Communications Minister Richard Alston has been unable to negotiate a deal between Telstra and Optus to share network rollouts. Alston has threatened to impose stringent rules from next July, which both carriers claim would impede their rollout and limit competition in the deregulated market. Page 3.

Although the Malaysian High Court ruled that last week's conference in Kuala Lumpur on East Timor was not banned, the Australian Government has indicated it still believes the meeting was in fact illegal. Both Prime Minister John Howard and Foreign Affais Minister Alexander Downer has refused to condemn the expulsion of 46 foreign conference participants by the Malaysian Government. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard said yesterday that Australia and the United States had a shared "destiny and future" in the Asia-Pacific region. On the eve of United States President Bill Clinton's visit to Australia, Howard said he would discuss ways to continue the momentum of trade liberalisation with Clinton when they meet on Wednesday. Page 1.

David Dicks, 18, sailed into Fremantle yesterday after becoming the youngest person to sail non-stop single-handedly around the world. Dicks appeared overwhelmed by his welcome yesterday, after being able to handle monstrous seas and conditions on his voage that would test the most seasoned of yachtsmen. Page 1.

The Federal Government will push for a A$24-a-week pay rise - three A$8 instalments over three years - for over one million of Australia's lowest paid workers from March next year. However, the increase assumes an inflation rate of two percent, compared with a Budget forecast of 2.75 percent. Page 1.

Australian soccer figures are unimpressed by the prospect of former England manager Terry Veneables accepting a A$420,000 per year offer to coach Australia's national side, the Socceroos. While a spokesman for Soccer Australia insisted the deal was not yet finalised, England's News of the World quoted Veneables as saying he was 99 percent certain in the position. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Council on the Cost of Government yesterday released a damning report into the New South Wales police service that outlines massive inefficiencies within the force and recommends the closure of 107 stations. Government sources indicated merging stations was the most obvious method of cutting overheads and meeting the central reform of having more police on the streets. Page 1.

The ACTU has dismissed the Federal Government's push to increase the wages of up to two million low-paid workers by A$24 a week - paid in three rounds over the next three years - saying it is a 'joke' that exposed the government's claim to represent the 'battlers'. Meanwhile, employers said the increase was too high. Page 1.

On the eve of crucial talks with U.S. President Bill Clinton, Prime Minister John Howard has defended controversial Government assistance to exporters. Howard also conceded the government would need to cope with reconciling the dual goals o reducing tariffs and maintaining a viable car industry. Page 1.

Perth's David Dicks, 18, received a warm welcome from 60,000 well-wishers at Fremantle yesterday after becoming the youngest person to circumnavigate the globe solo and non-stop. Dicks faced gales, snow, icebergs, fly swarms and damaged equipment during the 264 days on his 10-metre sloop Seaflight. Page 1.
THE AGE

The Federal Government will introduce strict new privacy legislation next year to crack down on the increased use of private-sector computer databases holding sensitive information on thousands of individuals. The databases are operated on behalf of real state agents, insurance companies and the health services industry. Page 1.

As part of the ACTU's "living wage" claim, the Federal Government will ask the Australian Industrial Relations Commission to approve the cumulative A$24 a week pay rise for low-paid workers who remain covered by award rates at less than average weekly earnings. The three annual $8-a-week wage rises are less than the hefty pay rises sought by the ACTU. Page 1.

The Australian film Shine, a portrayal of the life of virtuoso pianist David Helfgott, has caused Helfgott's sister Margaret to call for a public apology from the film's director Scott Hicks for the portrayal of Helfgott's father, Peter, as physically and emotionally brutal. Peter Helfgott's widow was also distressed and called for a more prominent display of the disclaimer that acknowledges the film is fiction. Page 1.

A parent from Auburn Primary School in Hawthorn who complained to Victoria Education Minister Phil Gude was sent a copy of an internal Education Department memo reassuring schools they can operate as normal after the November 29 deadline for merger plans even if they decide not to merge. Page 3.
